messages:
alex: Quick question — we're planning to deprecate the implicit default model pinning behavior (the server-side default that picks a variant when no pin header is provided). Need alignment on the contract for unpinned requests and the deprecation plan.

maria: +1 we should be conservative. Many clients assume "no header = stable default". Breaking that silently will bite mobile/web.

devon: Agreed. Proposal: introduce an explicit header so clients can opt into new behavior, keep current default for now, and then deprecate with warnings. Canary first. :thumbsup:

alex: Here's a concrete suggestion for negotiation headers:
```
Accept-Model-Version: pinned | latest | compatible
X-Requested-Model: model-name:vX.Y
X-Model-Pin: model-name@sha256
```
If `Accept-Model-Version` omitted, treat as legacy (current default) for the deprecation window.

cheng: We should avoid returning 4xx for unpinned clients. Fallback semantics: if a pin is requested but not available, fallback to a compatible variant (and emit metric `pin.fallback`) instead of erroring. That keeps apps online.

sam: Who will own SDK warnings? We should add a client-side console/log warning when server responds with `Deprecation-Warning` header. I can add warnings to JS/Python SDKs.

devon: I'd add a tenant-level feature flag (api.beta.model_pin=true) so we can enable the new header behavior per account during the canary. PR would add config check in the routing layer and a header passthrough.

maria: Timeline idea: 2 weeks canary (opt-in tenants), then server emits `Deprecation-Warning` for 30 days to all unpinned requests, then start rejecting unpinned requests unless tenant has explicitly opted in to legacy. Is 30 days long enough for large customers?

alex: Sounds reasonable as a default. For large enterprise customers we'll extend case-by-case. We must publish a deprecation notice + migration guide.

release-bot: Created issue REDWOOD-PI-4123: "default-model-pin deprecation + headers" and linked to changelog draft. Assignee: devon.

devon: I'll own the infra PR. Plan:
- add `api.beta.model_pin` tenant flag
- implement header parsing and fallback routing
- emit `Deprecation-Warning` and `X-Model-Selection` metadata header
- add integration tests and a contract test that validates legacy behavior still works when flag off
ETA: first PR by EOD Wed.

cheng: Two asks for the rollout checklist:
1) Ensure we log `pin.requested`, `pin.fallback`, `pin.succeeded` with sample rates and propagate trace id in `X-Trace-Id` header for debugging.
2) Add a perf/latency dashboard compare before/after for the canary tenants.

sam: I'll add SDK handling for `Deprecation-Warning` and `X-Model-Selection` asap. Will also include a small migration snippet in release notes.

maria: Don't forget docs: API reference for the new headers + quick migration guide (curl, SDKs). I'll slot a docs PR for Thurs.

alex: Perfect. devon, when you open the PR, add a short section in the description with the rollback steps (toggle tenant flag off, route back to default runtime). Also tag @cheng for telemetry checks.

devon: Will do. I'll include a small smoke test that asserts `X-Model-Selection` header exists and that fallback metric increments when we simulate an unavailable variant.

alex: Thanks all. If anyone has strong objections to the guardrails above call it out now; otherwise I'll draft the deprecation notice to be reviewed by legal/commms.

maria: No objections from me. :+1:

cheng: No objections. add me to the canary watchlist.

sam: OK from SDK side.

alex: Great — I'll post the draft notice tomorrow and link the issue. Thanks!
